evidence.quote:
## Joint content interpretation

The working comparison joins a botanical material register on f88r, botanical
description on f17r, differentiated water applications or bodily powers on
f77r, and member/status inscriptions on f72r. A common property vocabulary
could connect them without turning every plant into an ingredient or every
star-holder into a literal patient. A compendium with different genres remains
a serious alternative to one shared explanatory system.

This historical architecture is not a new codebook identification. The
[source notes](src/F77_HISTORICAL_READING.md) distinguish the actual dates and
layers of the medicinal-water, Wellcome MS510 and Parker MS395 comparators.
They support plausible kinds of content, not an EVA-to-Latin mapping.

The complete-page comparison sharpens possible referents and interpretation
burdens. It supplies zero confirmed lexemes, free components or plaintext
clauses. Smooth German would still require unsupported choices; the dictionary
and existing renderer therefore remain unchanged.

## The most useful joint interpretation

Try a collection describing **natural substances, their properties and bodily
effects, together with celestial correspondences or timing**. Some entries
may prescribe preparations, but not every line or inscription is an action.
The same written vocabulary can serve different subjects without changing a
property's meaning: a plant, a celestial figure and a bodily condition could
all carry an attribute such as hot or moist. That is a possibility, not an
identification of a particular Voynich form with those attributes.

cards.claim: GDT818 fixes four sentence models by crossing solkeey=steam/basin with chedy=becomes/contains, otherwise retaining R and leaving ol unknown. The completed local ZL3b/IT2a trial is Dessen [Dampf/Becken] [wird/enthält] Wasser, wenn die Luft kalt ist. Contains means physical contents, not filling or elemental potency: water may already be inside or newly arise. Basin contains water is plausible; basin becomes water is not ordinary filling; steam contains water requires a precise material account rather than blanket dismissal. The four closing word values and syntax were guessed, RF1b remains incomplete, and older Q/humoral rivals stay separate.

```text
solkeey okaiin chedy qokain sheedy qokaiin chedaiin chealy
Dampf?  dessen? wird? Wasser? wenn? Luft?  ist?     kalt?
```

„Dessen Dampf wird Wasser, wenn die Luft kalt ist.“ Die vier Schlusswerte
wurden zur Vervollständigung geraten; weder Wortbedeutung noch Syntax belegt.
RF: wenn? [qotaiin] [che] [aiin] kalt? bleibt unvollständig.

Hauptvergleich4fest: solkeey=Dampf/Becken × chedy=wird/enthält. R sonst gleich,
ol unbekannt; alte Q/humorale und andere Rivalen bleiben separat bestehen.
Enthält meint physischen Inhalt, nie Füllen oder bloße Elementpotenz. Wasser
kann schon enthalten sein oder erst entstehen; das trennt die Sachmodelle.
Becken enthält Wasser plausibel, Becken wird Wasser keine normale Füllung.
Dampf enthält Wasser braucht einen präzisen Stoffbegriff, nicht pauschal unmöglich.
